subject: Accounting
title: Current vs. Non-Current Assets
description: A short lesson to help you apply Current vs. Non-Current Assets.

hook.text: Cash in the register and a ten-year-old factory are both assets—but they behave very differently.

buildup.text: Current assets can be converted to cash within a year: cash, receivables, inventory.

discovery.text: Non-current assets last longer: property, equipment, patents, and goodwill.

twist.text: A company with lots of non-current assets but little cash can't pay its bills tomorrow.

climax.text: Analysts compare current assets to current liabilities to judge short-term survival.

punchline.text: Long-term wealth means nothing if you can't pay today.

quiz.question: What defines a current asset?
options: It can be converted to cash within a year
It lasts more than five years

details.summary: The balance sheet divides assets into current (convertible to cash within one year) and non-current (held longer term). This topic explains the classification, why it matters for liquidity analysis, and what each category reveals about a company's business model.
details.whyItMatters: The split between current and non-current assets reveals whether a company can meet its short-term obligations and how capital-intensive its business model is. It's fundamental to assessing financial health.
takeaways: Current assets include cash, receivables, and inventory—items expected to convert to cash within 12 months
Non-current assets include property, equipment, and intangibles—long-term investments in the business
A company with mostly current assets is asset-light; one with mostly non-current is capital-intensive

faq.question: What is the difference between current and non-current assets?
faq.answer: Current assets are expected to be converted to cash or consumed within one year—like cash, accounts receivable, and inventory. Non-current assets provide value over multiple years—like buildings, equipment, patents, and long-term investments.

faq.question: Why does the current vs. non-current distinction matter?
faq.answer: It reveals liquidity: can the company pay its bills? Current assets fund current liabilities. It also shows business model: a software company has mostly current assets, while a manufacturer has heavy non-current assets requiring ongoing capital investment.
